items.stem: In an experiment to characterize a nickel-metal-hydride battery pack, a variable resistor is adjusted while recording terminal potential difference V and current I from 0.0 A to 2.0 A. The resulting best-fit line is shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 10.6 V. (b) Gradient = (5 − 10.6) / 2 = -2.80 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(10.6 + 5) = 7.80 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 10.6 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (5 − 10.6) / 2 including negative sign.
Obtains -2.80 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(10.6 + 5) or area divided by 2 A.
Obtains 7.80 V.

items.stem: A charged capacitor in an analog integrator bleeder discharges through a fixed 25 kΩ resistor. The linear plot of ln(V / V) against time t passes through the vertical intercept (0 s, 2.140) and the endpoint (25 s, 0.140).
items.workedSolution: (a) taking natural logarithms gives a straight line with negative gradient equal to minus the reciprocal of the time constant and vertical intercept equal to the natural logarithm of the initial potential difference. (b) Gradient m = -0.08000 s⁻¹, so τ = −1/m = 12.50 s ≈ 12.5 s. (c) C = τ/R = 500 μF. (d) uses all measured data points along a straight best fit line rather than estimating a single tangent by eye.

markScheme.criterion: Shows taking natural logs produces a linear relation between ln(V) and t.
Identifies gradient = −1/τ and vertical intercept = ln(V₀).
Evaluates negative gradient m = -0.0800 s⁻¹ and uses τ = −1/m.
Correct time constant τ = 12.5 s.
Correct capacitance C = τ / R = 500 μF.
States that it uses all measured data points along a straight best fit line rather than estimating a single tangent by eye.

parts.prompt: Explain why plotting the natural logarithm of potential difference against time yields a straight line, identifying the physical meaning of its gradient and vertical intercept.
parts.expectedAnswer: From the exponential discharge equation, taking natural logarithms gives a straight line with negative gradient equal to minus the reciprocal of the time constant and vertical intercept equal to the natural logarithm of the initial potential difference.
workingSteps: Take natural logarithms of both sides of the exponential decay equation.
Compare with a linear equation to identify the negative gradient and the vertical intercept.

parts.prompt: Determine the time constant τ of the RC circuit from the gradient of the graph.
workingSteps: Time constant τ = −1 / m = 12.50 s ≈ 12.5 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the capacitance of the capacitor in μF given R = 25 kΩ.
State why determining τ from the gradient of a ln(V) against t graph is more reliable than drawing an initial tangent to a V against t curve.
parts.expectedAnswer: The logarithmic gradient method is more reliable because it uses all measured data points along a straight best fit line rather than estimating a single tangent by eye.
workingSteps: Drawing a tangent to a curve by eye is subjective and sensitive to noise at a single point, whereas a linear best-fit averages random errors over all readings.

items.stem: Examine the 12.0 s velocity–time curve for an underground mine haulage skip (initial coordinate 30.0 m from the shaft loading datum). What mean speed is achieved during this movement?
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(12 + 5)(14) = 119 m (independent of the 30 m starting offset). Mean speed = 119 / 12 = 9.92 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (119 m) by 12 s to obtain 9.92 m s⁻¹ (B).

options.distractorRationale: Takes half of the peak velocity as if there were no constant-speed cruise plateau.

items.stem: Determine the strain energy stored per unit volume (in MJ m⁻³) when a synthetic polyurethane tendon cord is loaded from zero strain to 0.4 along the plotted stress–strain curve (proportional limit at 0.2).
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.2)(120) + ½(120 + 180)(0.2) = 42.0 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 42.0 MJ m⁻³ (C).

items.stem: Varying centre-to-centre separation up to r⁻² = 80.0 m⁻² for nickel-plated hollow spheres suspended over an analytical balance yields the linear F versus r⁻² trace shown. Evaluate the slope ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.4 N; at r⁻² = 80 m⁻², F = 2.4 N. Gradient = (2.4 − 0.4) / 80 = 0.0250 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.4 N to get (2.4 − 0.4) / 80 = 0.0250 N m² (C).

items.stem: The potential difference–current characteristic for a vacuum-tube heater filament is plotted up to I = 1.0 A. What is the electrical resistance of the component when the current through it is 1.0 A?
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 1 A, V = 13.5 V, so R = 13.5 / 1 = 13.5 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 13.5 / 1 = 13.5 Ω (A).

items.stem: During uncertainty analysis of a piezoelectric load-cell calibration, the steepest worst-fit line is constructed across the domain 0.5 N to 2.5 N. Determine the gradient of the plotted line.
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 0.5 N, y₁ = 1.2 mV; at x₂ = 2.5 N, y₂ = 8.4 mV. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (8.4 − 1.2) / (2.5 − 0.5) = 3.60 mV N⁻¹.

options.distractorRationale: Computes the secant y₂ / x₂ as though the worst-fit line passed through the origin (0, 0) rather than (x₁, y₁).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts y₁ in the numerator but divides by x₂ instead of the horizontal span (x₂ − x₁).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δx / Δy instead of evaluating Δy / Δx.

items.stem: The false-origin experimental graph for a long copper strain-gauge wire starts both axes away from zero using red axis breaks. Why does NCUK practical graphing require a suppressed origin when all plotted data lie far from zero?
items.workedSolution: On a suppressed-origin NCUK graph, the procedure expands the plotted data to fill more than half of the grid improving reading precision.

markScheme.criterion: States accurately that the graphing technique expands the plotted data to fill more than half of the grid improving reading precision.

options.label: A
options.text: Because it expands the plotted data to fill more than half of the grid improving reading precision

options.label: B
options.text: It forces the y intercept on the false axis to equal the true zero-load constant directly
options.distractorRationale: Reading the vertical intercept off a false x-origin gives an incorrect offset value.

options.label: C
options.text: It eliminates all systematic zero error from the measuring instruments automatically
options.distractorRationale: Axis scaling changes graphical readability, not instrumental zero error.

options.label: D
options.text: It guarantees that the line of best fit passes straight through the bottom-left corner
options.distractorRationale: A suppressed-origin line rarely passes through the false corner point.

items.stem: In a kinematics linearization lab (take g = 9.81 m s⁻²), a dual-photogate brass cylinder released past an upper light gate on a frictionless slope with sin θ = 0.3 passes s = 0.0 m at speed u₀ and continues to s = 2.0 m. Determine the gradient of the plotted v² versus s graph.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 1.5 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 13.272 m² s⁻². Gradient = (13.272 − 1.5) / 2 = 2(9.81)(0.3) = 5.89 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 1.5 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.3) to get 5.89 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: Using the complete 10.0 s displacement–time trace for a telescope secondary-mirror actuator on its axial mount, calculate the average velocity over the entire 10.0 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Initial displacement at t = 0.0 s is 5 m and final displacement at t = 10 s is 13 m. Average velocity = (13 − 5) / 10 = 0.800 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates net displacement (13 − 5) / 10 = 0.800 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.distractorRationale: Uses final coordinate s₂ / t₃ and forgets to subtract the non-zero starting coordinate s₀.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Sums outward and return path lengths to compute average speed rather than net average velocity.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Takes the unweighted arithmetic mean of the two non-zero stage velocities, ignoring stage durations and the dwell plateau.

items.stem: A student plots current I (y-axis) against potential difference V (x-axis) for a uniform kanthal wire of length 1.00 m and cross-sectional area 5.80 × 10⁻⁸ m². The straight line of best fit passes through the origin and the point (10.0 V, 0.400 A). What is the resistivity of the kanthal?
items.workedSolution: Gradient m = ΔI / ΔV = 0.4000 A / 10.00 V = 0.04000 A V⁻¹. Since gradient = 1/R, R = 1/m = 25.00 Ω. Therefore ρ = R A / L = 1.450 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m ≈ 1.45 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses R = 1 / gradient and ρ = R A / L to obtain 1.45 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m.

items.stem: Static loading of a seismometer suspension spring produces the force–compression line up to 0.5 m. Held at 0.5 m compression against a 0.25 kg carriage on a smooth level guideway, it is then released.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies k as the gradient ΔF / Δx.
Obtains k = 120 N m⁻¹.
Uses triangular area ½Fx.
Obtains E_p = 15.0 J.
Equates ½(0.25)v² to stored elastic energy from (b).
Obtains v = 11.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Refer to the signed velocity–time graph for a magnetic-levitation shuttle pod travelling on a horizontal vacuum test guideway. Determine the resultant displacement after 12.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Velocity reaches zero at t = 8 s. Positive area = 96.0 m and area below the axis has magnitude 28.0 m. Net displacement = 96.0 − 28.0 = 68.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts reverse area (28.0 m) from forward area (96.0 m) to obtain 68.0 m (B).

items.workedSolution: (a) R = V / I = 8.000 Ω ≈ 8.00 Ω. (b) connect a potential divider with a series protective resistor an ammeter in series and a voltmeter in parallel across the component and reverse the supply connections for negative readings. (c) resistance decreases as light intensity increases because more charge carriers are released so the curve becomes steeper.

parts.prompt: Calculate the static resistance of the component at the highlighted operating point.
workingSteps: Recall that static resistance at a point is R = V / I (not the inverse of the local tangent).
Substitute V = 6.000 V and I = 0.7500 A to obtain R = 8.000 Ω ≈ 8.00 Ω.

parts.prompt: Describe the circuit arrangement and experimental procedure used to obtain a complete I–V characteristic safely across positive and negative potential differences.
parts.expectedAnswer: To obtain the full characteristic safely, connect a potential divider with a series protective resistor an ammeter in series and a voltmeter in parallel across the component and reverse the supply connections for negative readings.
workingSteps: Use a potential divider to vary potential difference smoothly from zero while limiting excessive current with a protective resistor.
Measure current with a series ammeter, potential difference with a parallel voltmeter, and reverse the supply leads for negative polarity.

parts.prompt: Explain the physical shape of the I–V characteristic in terms of charge carriers and resistance.
parts.expectedAnswer: The curve shows that the component resistance decreases as light intensity increases because more charge carriers are released so the curve becomes steeper.
workingSteps: Link the changing ratio of potential difference to current directly to the microscopic conduction mechanism.

items.stem: The graph shows how charge Q and potential difference V vary as an experiment charging capacitor is charged uniformly from zero up to Q = 3.00 mC at V = 12.0 V.
items.workedSolution: (a) Capacitance is the charge stored per unit potential difference across the plates. (b) C = Q / V = 250 μF. (c) Triangular area E = ½ Q V = 0.01800 J ≈ 0.0180 J.

markScheme.criterion: States charge stored per unit potential difference across the plates.
Correct capacitance 250 μF.
Recognises triangular area E = ½ Q V and converts mC to C.
Correct stored energy 0.0180 J.

parts.prompt: Define capacitance.
parts.expectedAnswer: Capacitance is the charge stored per unit potential difference across the plates.
workingSteps: State the definition as the ratio of charge stored to potential difference.

parts.prompt: Deduce the capacitance of the capacitor from the graph in μF.
Determine the electrical energy stored in the capacitor using the shaded triangular area under the graph.
workingSteps: Because V increases linearly from 0 to V_max as charge builds up, energy stored equals the triangular area E = ½ Q V.

items.stem: Use the signed 12.0 s acceleration–time graph to find the terminal upward velocity of a deep-sea winch capsule, which starts at 18.0 m s⁻¹ when t = 0.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Positive a–t area (0 to 6 s) = 36.0 m s⁻¹; negative area magnitude (6 s to 12 s) = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Net Δv = 36.0 − 18.0 = 18.0 m s⁻¹. Final velocity = 18 + (18.0) = 36.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Combines net signed area (18.0 m s⁻¹) with u₀ = 18 m s⁻¹ to obtain 36.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Moving forward from x = 0.0 m with initial speed 5.0 m s⁻¹, a warehouse pallet shuttle (mass 5.0 kg) is subjected to the resultant force–displacement profile shown up to x = 16.0 m. How much net work is done on it over the 16.0 m displacement?
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 14 m) = 200 J; resistive work (14 m to 16 m) = −5.00 J. Net work = 200 − 5.00 = 195 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (5.00 J) from positive trapezium (200 J) to get 195 J (B).

items.stem: Along a horizontal guideway, an ice-rink calibration sled of mass 1.0 kg moves in a fixed direction. Its momentum–time graph shows an impulse stage from t = 2.0 s to t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (9 − 3) / (6 − 2) = 1.50 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (9² − 3²) / (2 × 1) = 36.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 1.50 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 3 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 9 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 1 kg.
Obtains W = 36.0 J.

items.stem: Two-wire resistance readings R across a carbon-loaded antistatic composite bar include a fixed fixture offset R₀ when graphed against L / A from zero to 250.0 m⁻¹. Evaluate the resistivity ρ in Ω m.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (35 − 5) / 250 = 0.120 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 5 Ω to obtain ρ = (35 − 5) / 250 = 0.120 Ω m (C).

items.stem: Over load currents uniformly spanning 0.0 A to 0.8 A, an alkaline lantern battery exhibits the linear V–I plot shown. Calculate the average terminal potential difference across the plotted interval.
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 4.2 V at I = 0.0 A to 2.2 V at I = 0.8 A, so V_mean = ½(4.2 + 2.2) = 3.20 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(4.2 + 2.2) = 3.20 V (D).

items.stem: A capacitor in a bench capacitor discharge rig discharges through a resistor R = 25 kΩ. The straight-line graph of ln(V / V) against t passes through (0 s, 2.079) and (20 s, 0.079). What is the capacitance of the capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Gradient m = (0.079 − 2.079) / (20 − 0) = -0.1000 s⁻¹. Time constant τ = −1/m = 10.00 s. Capacitance C = τ / R = 10.00 s / (25 × 10³ Ω) = 400 μF.

markScheme.criterion: Extracts linearized graph parameters accurately to obtain 400 μF.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a high-speed bottling-line transfer sled rests at a position 25.0 m ahead of an optical home flag. The velocity–time graph shows its forward motion over 10.0 s, with uniform braking applied from t = 7.0 s until t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(10 + 5)(16) = 120 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 25 + 120 = 145 m. (c) Mean speed = 120 / 10 = 12.0 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 16) / (10 − 7) = -5.33 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 120 m.
Adds 25 m offset to obtain 145 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 10 s.
Obtains mean speed = 12.0 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -5.33 m s⁻².

workingSteps: Distance equals the trapezium area under the v–t curve.

Determine the mean speed over the 10.0 s run.
Calculate the acceleration between t = 7.0 s and t = 10.0 s.

items.stem: A tensile testing machine stretches an extruded fluoropolymer ribbon up to a strain of 0.8, producing the stress–strain curve shown. The limit of proportionality occurs at strain 0.4.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 170 / 0.4 = 425 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.4)(170) + ½(170 + 240)(0.4) = 116 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.4.
Obtains E = 425 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 116 MJ m⁻³.

parts.prompt: Determine the Young's modulus of the specimen over the proportional region (0.0 to 0.4).
Calculate the work done per unit volume in stretching the specimen from zero strain to 0.8.
workingSteps: Area from 0 to 0.4 = ½(0.4)(170) = 34.0 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: Because the force sensor has an unzeroed tare reading F₀, a student graphs total force F against r⁻² up to 60.0 m⁻² for insulated aluminium spheres monitored by a strain-gauge beam.

items.stem: During data analysis for an optical photodiode irradiance calibration, opposite ends of the uncertainty bars at 4.0 mW and 20.0 mW are joined to form the shallowest worst-fit line below.
items.workedSolution: (a) At 20 mW, y₂ = 52.0 μA. (b) Worst-fit gradient = (52 − 12) / (20 − 4) = 2.50 μA mW⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Reads y₂ = 52.0 μA.
Reads y₁ = 12 μA at x₁ = 4 mW and forms Δy / Δx.
Subtracts x₁ = 4 mW in the denominator (20 − 4).
Obtains 2.50 μA mW⁻¹.

items.stem: A student investigates a tensioned constantan test wire and plots the suppressed-origin graph shown, with vertical error bars of ±0.14 mm. Two widely separated coordinates on the line of best fit are (20.0 N, 2.760 mm) and (60.0 N, 4.840 mm). The steepest straight line still passing through all error bars has gradient 0.04360 mm N⁻¹. The specimen diameter is measured as d = 0.48 ± 0.012 mm.
items.workedSolution: (a) m_best = (4.840 − 2.760) / (60.0 − 20.0) = 0.05200 mm N⁻¹ ≈ 0.0520 mm N⁻¹. (b) Δm = |0.04360 − 0.05200| = 8.40 × 10⁻³ mm N⁻¹. (c) A suppressed origin expands the plotted data to fill more than half of the grid improving reading precision. (d) %Δm = 16.15%, %ΔA = 2 × %Δd = 5.000%, total = 21.15% ≈ 21.2%.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly substitutes large-triangle coordinates (4.840 − 2.760) / (60.0 − 20.0).
Obtains best-fit gradient = 0.0520 mm N⁻¹ with correct compound SI unit.
Calculates Δm = |m_worst − m_best| = 8.40 × 10⁻³ mm N⁻¹.
States that a false origin expands the plotted data to fill more than half of the grid improving reading precision.
Evaluates %Δm = 16.2% and %ΔA = 2 × %Δd = 5.00%.
Sums percentage uncertainties to obtain 21.2%.

items.stem: The Cartesian plot shows experimental (V, I) data and the straight line of best fit for a uniform titanium wire of length 2.00 m and cross-sectional area 8.40 × 10⁻⁸ m². The line of best fit passes through the origin and reaches I = 0.500 A at V = 5.00 V.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resistivity is the resistance of a sample of unit length and unit cross sectional area. (b) Gradient = 0.1000 A V⁻¹, so R = 1 / gradient = 10.0 Ω. (c) ρ = RA/L = 4.200 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m ≈ 4.20 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States resistance of a sample of unit length and unit cross sectional area.
Correctly specifies all quantities (or notes constant temperature / material property).
Computes large-triangle gradient m = ΔI/ΔV = 0.100 A V⁻¹ and takes its reciprocal R = 1/m.
Correct wire resistance R = 10.0 Ω.
Substitutes R, A, and L correctly into ρ = RA/L.
Correct resistivity 4.20 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m with unit Ω m.

parts.prompt: Calculate the resistivity of the alloy, stating the appropriate SI unit.
workingSteps: Evaluate ρ = 4.200 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m ≈ 4.20 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m.

items.stem: Within its Hookean limit, an optical-mount preload spring produces the force–extension graph shown up to an extension of 0.4 m. How much elastic potential energy is stored at x = 0.4 m?
items.workedSolution: Elastic potential energy equals the triangular area under the F–x line: E_p = ½ F x = ½(64)(0.4) = 12.8 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes triangular area ½(64)(0.4) = 12.8 J (C).

items.stem: The graph displays how the velocity of a linear-motor camera dolly on a studio optical bench varies with time over 16.0 s. Positive velocity corresponds to motion northward, and direction reversal occurs during the linear ramp between t = 8.0 s and t = 12.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 11 s. Positive area = 90.0 m and unsigned negative area = 18.0 m, giving total distance = 108 m. (b) Net displacement = 90.0 − 18.0 = 72.0 m; average velocity = 72.0 / 16 = 4.50 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−4 − 12) / (12 − 8) = -4.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 11 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (90.0 m and 18.0 m).
Obtains total distance = 108 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (72.0 m) and divides by 16 s.
Obtains average velocity = 4.50 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -4.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total distance travelled between t = 0.0 s and t = 16.0 s.
workingSteps: Velocity crosses zero at t = 11 s; forward area = 90.0 m.
Unsigned reverse area = 18.0 m, so total distance = 90.0 + 18.0 = 108 m.

parts.prompt: Determine the net displacement and hence calculate the average velocity over the 16.0 s interval.
workingSteps: Average velocity = Δs / Δt = 72.0 / 16 = 4.50 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Travelling in a straight line with initial momentum 10.0 kg m s⁻¹, a ballistic pendulum carriage of mass 2.5 kg is acted upon by a collinear controlled gas-jet pulse for 1.0 s, as shown on the force–time graph.
items.workedSolution: (a) Impulse J = ½(1 + 0.6)(60) = 48.0 N s. (b) Final momentum p_f = 10 + 48.0 = 58.0 kg m s⁻¹. (c) Speed increase Δv = 48.0 / 2.5 = 19.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes impulse from the trapezium area under the F–t curve.
Obtains J = 48.0 N s.
Adds 10 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 58.0 kg m s⁻¹.
Divides impulse from (a) by 2.5 kg.
Obtains Δv = 19.2 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The I–V characteristic graph for a green indicator diode highlights an operating point where V = 2.40 V and I = 20 mA. What is the static resistance of the component at this operating point?
items.workedSolution: Static resistance at any point on an I–V graph is R = V / I = 2.400 V / 0.02000 A = 120.0 Ω ≈ 120 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates R = V / I accurately to obtain 120 Ω.

items.stem: The charging graph for a camera-flash capacitor is a straight line from the origin to Q = 6.00 mC at V = 15.0 V. What is the capacitance of the capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Convert Q = 6 mC = 6.000 × 10⁻³ C. Capacitance C = Q / V = 4.000 × 10⁻⁴ F = 400 μF.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly converts mC to C and obtains 400 μF.

items.stem: Engineers monitor a maglev propulsion test pod for 12.0 s starting from an initial eastward velocity of 12.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, obtaining the piecewise acceleration–time graph below.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s. (b) Positive area = 25.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 12 + 25.0 = 37.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 9.00 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 37.0 − 9.00 = 28.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 6.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 6 s (25.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 12 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 37.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (9.00 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 28.0 m s⁻¹.

workingSteps: Acceleration changes from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate this maximum speed.
Calculate the velocity at t = 12.0 s.
workingSteps: Magnitude of negative a–t area (6 s to 12 s) = ½(3)(2) + (3)(2) = 9.00 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Force-transducer and encoder data for a magnetic-launch coaster bogie (mass 1.6 kg, speed 4.5 m s⁻¹ at x = 0.0 m) are plotted over a 8.0 m straight track.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates positive (54.0 J) and negative (−4.00 J) areas.
Obtains net work W = 50.0 J.
Uses ½mv² = ½(1.6)(4.5²) + W.
Obtains v = 9.10 m s⁻¹.
Divides net work by 8 m to get 6.25 N.

parts.prompt: Calculate the net work done on the 1.6 kg object between x = 0.0 m and x = 8.0 m.
workingSteps: Positive area (0 to 6 m) = ½(6 + 3)(12) = 54.0 J; negative area (6 m to 8 m) = −½(2)(4) = −4.00 J.

parts.prompt: Calculate its speed at x = 8.0 m.
State the mean resultant force over the 8.0 m displacement.

items.stem: In a linear dynamics experiment, a superconducting levitation carrier of mass 5.0 kg moves in a straight line with momentum varying as shown. How much net work is done on it between t = 2.0 s and t = 7.0 s?
items.workedSolution: Using E_k = p² / (2m), net work W = ΔE_k = (30² − 10²) / (2 × 5) = 80.0 J.

items.stem: In an electrical properties lab, resistance readings across a polypyrrole conductive polymer film are linearized against geometric factor L / A up to 400.0 m⁻¹, revealing a non-zero contact offset R₀.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 8.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (36 − 8) / 400 = 0.0700 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 8.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 8 Ω from 36 Ω before dividing by 400 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.0700 Ω m.

items.stem: The straight-line plot below shows how the terminal potential difference of a silver-oxide instrument battery falls as load current increases from 0.0 A to 4.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 13.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 13) / 4 = -1.50 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(13 + 7) = 10.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 13.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 13) / 4 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.50 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(13 + 7) or area divided by 4 A.
Obtains 10.0 V.

items.stem: A charged capacitor in a teaching capacitor discharge rig discharges through a fixed 20 kΩ resistor. The linear plot of ln(V / V) against time t passes through the vertical intercept (0 s, 1.872) and the endpoint (14 s, -0.128).
items.workedSolution: (a) taking natural logarithms gives a straight line with negative gradient equal to minus the reciprocal of the time constant and vertical intercept equal to the natural logarithm of the initial potential difference. (b) Gradient m = -0.1429 s⁻¹, so τ = −1/m = 7.000 s ≈ 7.00 s. (c) C = τ/R = 350 μF. (d) uses all measured data points along a straight best fit line rather than estimating a single tangent by eye.

markScheme.criterion: Shows taking natural logs produces a linear relation between ln(V) and t.
Identifies gradient = −1/τ and vertical intercept = ln(V₀).
Evaluates negative gradient m = -0.143 s⁻¹ and uses τ = −1/m.
Correct time constant τ = 7.00 s.
Correct capacitance C = τ / R = 350 μF.
States that it uses all measured data points along a straight best fit line rather than estimating a single tangent by eye.

parts.prompt: Explain why plotting the natural logarithm of potential difference against time yields a straight line, identifying the physical meaning of its gradient and vertical intercept.
parts.expectedAnswer: From the exponential discharge equation, taking natural logarithms gives a straight line with negative gradient equal to minus the reciprocal of the time constant and vertical intercept equal to the natural logarithm of the initial potential difference.
workingSteps: Take natural logarithms of both sides of the exponential decay equation.
Compare with a linear equation to identify the negative gradient and the vertical intercept.

parts.prompt: Determine the time constant τ of the RC circuit from the gradient of the graph.
workingSteps: Time constant τ = −1 / m = 7.000 s ≈ 7.00 s.

parts.prompt: Calculate the capacitance of the capacitor in μF given R = 20 kΩ.
State why determining τ from the gradient of a ln(V) against t graph is more reliable than drawing an initial tangent to a V against t curve.
parts.expectedAnswer: The logarithmic gradient method is more reliable because it uses all measured data points along a straight best fit line rather than estimating a single tangent by eye.
workingSteps: Drawing a tangent to a curve by eye is subjective and sensitive to noise at a single point, whereas a linear best-fit averages random errors over all readings.

items.stem: In the velocity–time record for an underground mine haulage skip (initially 38.0 m from the shaft loading datum), uniform braking begins at t = 12.0 s and ends at rest at t = 16.0 s. Find the signed braking acceleration.
items.workedSolution: During braking from t = 12 s to t = 16 s, a = (0 − 16) / (16 − 12) = -4.00 m s⁻².

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a synthetic polyurethane tendon cord stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.6 (kink at strain 0.3). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.6?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.3)(150) + ½(150 + 210)(0.3) = 76.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 76.5 MJ m⁻³ (D).

items.stem: How large is the slope ΔF / Δ(r⁻²) of the inverse-square linearization graph recorded up to 20.0 m⁻² using charged graphite-coated spheres on a quartz-fibre force sensor?
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N; at r⁻² = 20 m⁻², F = 0.7 N. Gradient = (0.7 − 0.1) / 20 = 0.0300 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.1 N to get (0.7 − 0.1) / 20 = 0.0300 N m² (D).

items.stem: At the upper plotted current I = 4.0 A, find the resistance of a tungsten filament indicator lamp from its potential difference–current characteristic.
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 4 A, V = 14 V, so R = 14 / 4 = 3.50 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 14 / 4 = 3.50 Ω (A).

items.stem: Inspect the steepest error-bar line of worst fit plotted from 1.0 A to 6.0 A for a Helmholtz-coil axial field check. What value does its gradient take?
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 1 A, y₁ = 3 mT; at x₂ = 6 A, y₂ = 22 mT. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (22 − 3) / (6 − 1) = 3.80 mT A⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (22 − 3) / (6 − 1) = 3.80 mT A⁻¹ (D).

options.distractorRationale: Subtracts y₁ in the numerator but divides by x₂ instead of the horizontal span (x₂ − x₁).

options.label: C

items.stem: For the calibrated bench force spring plotted with vertical error bars ±0.01 m on the suppressed-origin graph, the best-fit gradient is 0.01140 m N⁻¹ and the steepest acceptable worst-fit line passing through all error bars has gradient 9.900 × 10⁻³ m N⁻¹. What is the absolute uncertainty in the gradient?
items.workedSolution: Absolute uncertainty Δm = |m_worst − m_best| = |9.900 × 10⁻³ − 0.01140| = 1.500 × 10⁻³ m N⁻¹ ≈ 1.50 × 10⁻³ m N⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δm = |m_worst − m_best| = 1.50 × 10⁻³ m N⁻¹.

items.stem: An optical timer measures speed v of a card-carrying glider on an inclined linear air track at positions up to s = 2.5 m along a frictionless incline (sin θ = 0.2, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). What is the slope of the resulting v²–s graph?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² and at s = 2.5 m, v² = 12.61 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.61 − 2.8) / 2.5 = 2(9.81)(0.2) = 3.92 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.2) to get 3.92 m s⁻² (B).

items.stem: A sensor records the displacement–time graph of a coastal tide-gauge float along a vertical stilling tube. What is its signed velocity during the return stage between t = 10.0 s and t = 20.0 s?
items.workedSolution: From t = 10 s to t = 20 s, displacement changes from 73 m to 39 m. Velocity v = (39 − 73) / (20 − 10) = -3.40 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A student plots current I (y-axis) against potential difference V (x-axis) for a uniform cupronickel wire of length 1.50 m and cross-sectional area 7.20 × 10⁻⁸ m². The straight line of best fit passes through the origin and the point (5.00 V, 0.625 A). What is the resistivity of the cupronickel?
items.workedSolution: Gradient m = ΔI / ΔV = 0.6250 A / 5.000 V = 0.1250 A V⁻¹. Since gradient = 1/R, R = 1/m = 8.000 Ω. Therefore ρ = R A / L = 3.840 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m ≈ 3.84 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses R = 1 / gradient and ρ = R A / L to obtain 3.84 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m.

items.stem: The force–compression graph for a laboratory catapult tension spring is recorded up to a maximum compression of 0.5 m. The compressed spring is then released from rest on a smooth horizontal track to launch a 0.25 kg glider.

Obtains k = 80.0 N m⁻¹.
Uses triangular area ½Fx.
Obtains E_p = 10.0 J.
Equates ½(0.25)v² to stored elastic energy from (b).
Obtains v = 8.94 m s⁻¹.

options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δt / Δ(ln C) to obtain −1/λ (negative mean lifetime) instead of the gradient −λ.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes ln C drops to zero at t = t_max instead of subtracting the non-zero final ordinate ln C(t_max).

items.stem: The velocity–time profile shows an automated rail inspection trolley reversing motion along a straight viaduct rail with eastward defined as positive. Calculate the total scalar distance travelled between t = 0.0 s and t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: Velocity crosses zero at t = 7 s. Forward area (0 to 7 s) = ½(2)(16) + (3)(16) + ½(2)(16) = 80.0 m. Reverse area magnitude (7 s to 10 s) = ½(1)(8) + (2)(8) = 20.0 m. Total distance = 80.0 + 20.0 = 100 m.

markScheme.criterion: Sums unsigned positive (80.0 m) and negative (20.0 m) velocity–time areas to obtain 100 m (A).

items.stem: Before a 0.8 s cold-gas thruster burn, a cold-gas attitude probe of mass 2.0 kg has momentum 6.0 kg m s⁻¹. Using the force–time plot, find its momentum immediately after the pulse.
items.workedSolution: Impulse Δp = ½(0.8 + 0.4)(50) = 30.0 N s. Final momentum p_f = p₀ + Δp = 6 + 30.0 = 36.0 kg m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Adds impulse (30.0 N s) to p₀ = 6 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 36.0 kg m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The graph shows the I–V characteristic recorded for a tungsten torch filament in an NCUK laboratory investigation, with current plotted on the vertical axis and potential difference on the horizontal axis. At the highlighted operating point, V = 7.50 V and I = 0.600 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) R = V / I = 12.50 Ω ≈ 12.5 Ω. (b) connect a potential divider with a series protective resistor an ammeter in series and a voltmeter in parallel across the component and reverse the supply connections for negative readings. (c) resistance increases with potential difference because heating increases lattice ion vibration amplitude and electron collisions.

parts.prompt: Calculate the static resistance of the component at the highlighted operating point.
workingSteps: Recall that static resistance at a point is R = V / I (not the inverse of the local tangent).
Substitute V = 7.500 V and I = 0.6000 A to obtain R = 12.50 Ω ≈ 12.5 Ω.

parts.prompt: Describe the circuit arrangement and experimental procedure used to obtain a complete I–V characteristic safely across positive and negative potential differences.
parts.expectedAnswer: To obtain the full characteristic safely, connect a potential divider with a series protective resistor an ammeter in series and a voltmeter in parallel across the component and reverse the supply connections for negative readings.
workingSteps: Use a potential divider to vary potential difference smoothly from zero while limiting excessive current with a protective resistor.
Measure current with a series ammeter, potential difference with a parallel voltmeter, and reverse the supply leads for negative polarity.

parts.prompt: Explain the physical shape of the I–V characteristic in terms of charge carriers and resistance.
parts.expectedAnswer: The curve shows that the component resistance increases with potential difference because heating increases lattice ion vibration amplitude and electron collisions.
workingSteps: Link the changing ratio of potential difference to current directly to the microscopic conduction mechanism.

items.stem: The graph shows how charge Q and potential difference V vary as a stabiliser reservoir capacitor is charged uniformly from zero up to Q = 4.50 mC at V = 18.0 V.
items.workedSolution: (a) Capacitance is the charge stored per unit potential difference across the plates. (b) C = Q / V = 250 μF. (c) Triangular area E = ½ Q V = 0.04050 J ≈ 0.0405 J.

markScheme.criterion: States charge stored per unit potential difference across the plates.
Correct capacitance 250 μF.
Recognises triangular area E = ½ Q V and converts mC to C.
Correct stored energy 0.0405 J.

workingSteps: Because V increases linearly from 0 to V_max as charge builds up, energy stored equals the triangular area E = ½ Q V.

items.stem: Moving forward at 11.0 m s⁻¹ at t = 0.0 s, an aerotow winch launch carriage experiences the acceleration–time history plotted over 10.0 s. Find its peak speed.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 4 s). Positive area Δv_max = (2)(10) + ½(2)(10) = 30.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 11 + 30.0 = 41.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 4 s (30.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 11 m s⁻¹ to get 41.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Data loggers record the linear momentum of a linear air-bearing carriage (mass 3.0 kg), which experiences a constant resultant force between t = 2.0 s and t = 6.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resultant force F = Δp / Δt = (18 − 6) / (6 − 2) = 3.00 N. (b) Net work W = ΔE_k = (18² − 6²) / (2 × 3) = 48.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies resultant force as gradient Δp / Δt of the p–t graph.
Obtains F = 3.00 N.
Relates net work to ΔE_k = (p₂² − p₁²) / (2m).
Substitutes p₁ = 6 kg m s⁻¹, p₂ = 18 kg m s⁻¹, and m = 3 kg.
Obtains W = 48.0 J.

items.stem: Inspect the linear plot of measured resistance R versus L / A (spanning 0.0 m⁻¹ to 160.0 m⁻¹) for a polypyrrole conductive polymer film. What is the material's resistivity ρ?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (26 − 6) / 160 = 0.125 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 6 Ω to obtain ρ = (26 − 6) / 160 = 0.125 Ω m (A).

items.stem: By varying a rheostat connected to a nickel-metal-hydride battery pack, terminal voltage V is graphed against current I up to 4.0 A. Find the signed slope ΔV / ΔI.
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 15 V; at I = 4 A, V = 5 V. Gradient = (5 − 15) / 4 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates (5 − 15) / 4 = -2.50 V A⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: A capacitor in a laboratory discharge board discharges through a resistor R = 25 kΩ. The straight-line graph of ln(V / V) against t passes through (0 s, 2.398) and (30 s, 0.398). What is the capacitance of the capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Gradient m = (0.398 − 2.398) / (30 − 0) = -0.06667 s⁻¹. Time constant τ = −1/m = 15.00 s. Capacitance C = τ / R = 15.00 s / (25 × 10³ Ω) = 600 μF.

markScheme.criterion: Extracts linearized graph parameters accurately to obtain 600 μF.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a shipyard gantry crane crab rests at a position 25.0 m ahead of a western end-stop. The velocity–time graph shows its forward motion over 10.0 s, with uniform braking applied from t = 7.0 s until t = 10.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Trapezium area Δx = ½(10 + 5)(16) = 120 m. (b) Final distance from datum = 25 + 120 = 145 m. (c) Mean speed = 120 / 10 = 12.0 m s⁻¹. (d) Braking acceleration = (0 − 16) / (10 − 7) = -5.33 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Identifies distance travelled as the area under the v–t trapezium.
Obtains Δx = 120 m.
Adds 25 m offset to obtain 145 m.
Divides distance travelled from (a) by 10 s.
Obtains mean speed = 12.0 m s⁻¹.
Obtains braking acceleration = -5.33 m s⁻².

Determine the mean speed over the 10.0 s run.
Calculate the acceleration between t = 7.0 s and t = 10.0 s.

items.stem: In a materials laboratory, uniaxial tension applied to a braided aramid-polymer composite tape yields the bilinear stress–strain trace to strain 0.5, with proportional behaviour ending at 0.25.
items.workedSolution: (a) Young's modulus E = 180 / 0.25 = 720 MPa. (b) Energy per unit volume = ½(0.25)(180) + ½(180 + 260)(0.25) = 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial gradient σ / ε up to ε = 0.25.
Obtains E = 720 MPa.
Identifies work per unit volume as total area under the σ–ε graph.
Splits area into initial triangle plus upper trapezium.
Obtains 77.5 MJ m⁻³.

items.stem: Refer to the linearized Coulomb graph of balance reading F against r⁻² (up to 80.0 m⁻²) recorded using silvered glass spheres positioned above a digital load pan.
items.workedSolution: (a) At r⁻² = 0, systematic tare offset F₀ = 0.200 N. (b) Gradient = (2.2 − 0.2) / 80 = 0.0250 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads intercept F₀ = 0.200 N.
Evaluates ΔF = 2.2 − 0.2 using intercept from (a).
Divides ΔF by 80 m⁻² and states correct unit N m².
Obtains 0.0250 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Reads y₂ = 42.0 rad.

Obtains 2.75 rad N⁻¹ m⁻¹.

items.stem: A student investigates a stretched brass laboratory wire and plots the suppressed-origin graph shown, with vertical error bars of ±0.12 mm. Two widely separated coordinates on the line of best fit are (15.0 N, 2.120 mm) and (55.0 N, 3.880 mm). The steepest straight line still passing through all error bars has gradient 0.03680 mm N⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) m_best = (3.880 − 2.120) / (55.0 − 15.0) = 0.04400 mm N⁻¹ ≈ 0.0440 mm N⁻¹. (b) Δm = |0.03680 − 0.04400| = 7.20 × 10⁻³ mm N⁻¹. (c) A suppressed origin expands the plotted data to fill more than half of the grid improving reading precision.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly substitutes large-triangle coordinates (3.880 − 2.120) / (55.0 − 15.0).
Obtains best-fit gradient = 0.0440 mm N⁻¹ with correct compound SI unit.
Calculates Δm = |m_worst − m_best| = 7.20 × 10⁻³ mm N⁻¹.
States that a false origin expands the plotted data to fill more than half of the grid improving reading precision.

items.stem: The Cartesian plot shows experimental (V, I) data and the straight line of best fit for a uniform manganin wire of length 1.80 m and cross-sectional area 8.60 × 10⁻⁸ m². The line of best fit passes through the origin and reaches I = 0.600 A at V = 6.00 V.
items.workedSolution: (a) Resistivity is the resistance of a sample of unit length and unit cross sectional area. (b) Gradient = 0.1000 A V⁻¹, so R = 1 / gradient = 10.0 Ω. (c) ρ = RA/L = 4.778 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m ≈ 4.78 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States resistance of a sample of unit length and unit cross sectional area.
Correctly specifies all quantities (or notes constant temperature / material property).
Computes large-triangle gradient m = ΔI/ΔV = 0.100 A V⁻¹ and takes its reciprocal R = 1/m.
Correct wire resistance R = 10.0 Ω.
Substitutes R, A, and L correctly into ρ = RA/L.
Correct resistivity 4.78 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m with unit Ω m.

parts.expectedAnswer: Electrical resistivity is the resistance of a sample of unit length and unit cross sectional area, where resistance, cross-sectional area, and length are measured for a uniform specimen at constant temperature.
workingSteps: State the definition in terms of a conductor of unit length and unit cross-sectional area.
Identify that resistivity is an intrinsic property of the material at constant temperature.

workingSteps: Because I is on the vertical axis, R = 1 / m = 10.00 Ω ≈ 10.0 Ω.

parts.prompt: Calculate the resistivity of the alloy, stating the appropriate SI unit.
workingSteps: Evaluate ρ = 4.778 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m ≈ 4.78 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m.

items.stem: How many newtons per metre (k) are required to extend a laboratory catapult tension spring according to the Hookean graph spanning 0.0 m to 0.4 m?
items.workedSolution: Spring constant k = gradient ΔF / Δx = 80 / 0.4 = 200 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates gradient k = 80 / 0.4 = 200 N m⁻¹ (A).

items.stem: In a laboratory motion trial, a linear-motor camera dolly travels on a studio optical bench with northward taken as positive. The velocity–time graph records its motion from t = 0.0 s to t = 16.0 s, including uniform reversal thrust from t = 8.0 s to t = 12.0 s.
items.workedSolution: (a) Zero-velocity crossing is at t = 11 s. Positive area = 90.0 m and unsigned negative area = 18.0 m, giving total distance = 108 m. (b) Net displacement = 90.0 − 18.0 = 72.0 m; average velocity = 72.0 / 16 = 4.50 m s⁻¹. (c) Acceleration = (−4 − 12) / (12 − 8) = -4.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Finds zero-crossing t = 11 s and evaluates both unsigned areas (90.0 m and 18.0 m).
Obtains total distance = 108 m.
Subtracts areas for net displacement (72.0 m) and divides by 16 s.
Obtains average velocity = 4.50 m s⁻¹.
Obtains acceleration = -4.00 m s⁻² including negative sign.

parts.prompt: Determine the net displacement and hence calculate the average velocity over the 16.0 s interval.
workingSteps: Average velocity = Δs / Δt = 72.0 / 16 = 4.50 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: Travelling in a straight line with initial momentum 10.0 kg m s⁻¹, a microgravity cargo pod of mass 2.5 kg is acted upon by a collinear docking vernier firing for 1.0 s, as shown on the force–time graph.
items.workedSolution: (a) Impulse J = ½(1 + 0.6)(60) = 48.0 N s. (b) Final momentum p_f = 10 + 48.0 = 58.0 kg m s⁻¹. (c) Speed increase Δv = 48.0 / 2.5 = 19.2 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes impulse from the trapezium area under the F–t curve.
Obtains J = 48.0 N s.
Adds 10 kg m s⁻¹ to obtain 58.0 kg m s⁻¹.
Divides impulse from (a) by 2.5 kg.
Obtains Δv = 19.2 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The I–V characteristic graph shown (current I on the vertical axis against potential difference V on the horizontal axis) was recorded for a blue semiconductor emitter. Which physical explanation correctly describes the shape of this characteristic?
items.workedSolution: On an I–V graph (I on the vertical axis, V on the horizontal axis), gradient equals reciprocal of resistance. For this light emitting diode, conducts sharply above the forward threshold voltage and has very high resistance in reverse bias.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies that conducts sharply above the forward threshold voltage and has very high resistance in reverse bias.

items.stem: The straight-line charging graph for a pulse-discharge capacitor extends from (0, 0) to a final state of Q = 9.00 mC and V = 12.0 V. Using the area under the graph, what is the electrical energy stored in the capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Triangular area under the linear graph gives E = ½ Q V = 0.5 × (9 × 10⁻³ C) × 12 V = 0.05400 J ≈ 0.0540 J.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly converts mC to C and obtains 0.0540 J.

items.stem: During a 10.0 s test run, a high-rise express lift enters the instrumented section moving upward at 10.0 m s⁻¹. Its subsequent signed acceleration–time trace is shown.
items.workedSolution: (a) Maximum speed occurs when acceleration crosses zero from positive to negative at t = 6.00 s. (b) Positive area = 18.0 m s⁻¹, giving v_max = 10 + 18.0 = 28.0 m s⁻¹. (c) Negative area magnitude = 9.00 m s⁻¹, so v_final = 28.0 − 9.00 = 19.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: States t = 6.00 s.
Evaluates positive area up to 6 s (18.0 m s⁻¹) and adds u₀ = 10 m s⁻¹.
Obtains v_max = 28.0 m s⁻¹.
Subtracts negative area (9.00 m s⁻¹) from v_max.
Obtains final velocity = 19.0 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The graph displays the linear momentum of a low-friction dynamics trolley (mass 6.0 kg) against time. What resultant force acts on it between t = 4.0 s and t = 10.0 s?
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (36 − 12) / (10 − 4) = 4.00 N.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates F = Δp / Δt = (36 − 12) / (6) = 4.00 N (D).

options.distractorRationale: Computes the secant ratio p₂ / t₂ from the origin, ignoring both initial momentum p₁ and start time t₁.

options.distractorRationale: Divides Δp / Δt by mass m, obtaining acceleration rather than resultant force.

items.stem: The linear graph below displays total measured resistance R against L / A (0.0 m⁻¹ to 50.0 m⁻¹) during a resistivity test on a sintered silicon-carbide heating rod.
items.workedSolution: (a) Vertical intercept R₀ = 2.00 Ω. (b) Resistivity ρ = (14 − 2) / 50 = 0.240 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: States R₀ = 2.00 Ω.
Identifies ρ with the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A).
Subtracts R₀ = 2 Ω from 14 Ω before dividing by 50 m⁻¹.
Obtains ρ = 0.240 Ω m.

items.stem: To determine the EMF and internal resistance of a thermoelectric Seebeck generator, V is graphed against I over the current interval 0.0 A to 4.0 A.
items.workedSolution: (a) Open-circuit intercept gives ε = 13.0 V. (b) Gradient = (7 − 13) / 4 = -1.50 V A⁻¹. (c) Mean terminal p.d. = ½(13 + 7) = 10.0 V.

markScheme.criterion: Reads ε = 13.0 V at I = 0.
Evaluates (7 − 13) / 4 including negative sign.
Obtains -1.50 V A⁻¹.
Uses ½(13 + 7) or area divided by 4 A.
Obtains 10.0 V.

items.stem: A capacitor in a high-resistance bleeder network discharges through a 80 kΩ resistor. The linear plot of ln(V / V) against time t has a vertical intercept of 2.015 and passes through (32 s, 0.015). What is the initial potential difference V₀ across the capacitor at t = 0?
items.workedSolution: Since ln(V) = −t/τ + ln(V₀), the vertical intercept is ln(V₀) = 2.015. Taking the exponential gives V₀ = e^(2.015) = 7.500 V ≈ 7.50 V.

markScheme.criterion: Extracts linearized graph parameters accurately to obtain 7.50 V.

items.stem: Over a 16.0 s transfer starting at x = 35.0 m from the optical home flag, a high-speed bottling-line transfer sled has the velocity–time graph shown. Calculate its average speed over the 16.0 s interval.
items.workedSolution: Distance travelled Δx = ½(16 + 6)(19) = 209 m (independent of the 35 m starting offset). Mean speed = 209 / 16 = 13.1 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Divides trapezium distance (209 m) by 16 s to obtain 13.1 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The tensile stress–strain curve for an extruded fluoropolymer ribbon is linear from 0.0 to strain 0.5 and reaches strain 1.0. Determine the Young's modulus in MPa.
items.workedSolution: Up to the limit of proportionality at ε = 0.5, stress reaches 250 MPa. Young's modulus E = σ / ε = 250 / 0.5 = 500 MPa.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates initial linear gradient E = 250 / 0.5 = 500 MPa (D).

items.stem: Readings F from silvered glass spheres positioned above a digital load pan are linearized against r⁻² from 0.0 m⁻² to 40.0 m⁻². Accounting for the systematic zero-offset F₀, determine the gradient ΔF / Δ(r⁻²).
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.15 N; at r⁻² = 40 m⁻², F = 1.35 N. Gradient = (1.35 − 0.15) / 40 = 0.0300 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.15 N to get (1.35 − 0.15) / 40 = 0.0300 N m² (A).

items.stem: In a DC bench test, a platinum-wire hot-wire anemometer element exhibits the V–I graph shown up to 2.0 A. Evaluate its electrical resistance R = V / I when I = 2.0 A.
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 2 A, V = 16 V, so R = 16 / 2 = 8.00 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 16 / 2 = 8.00 Ω (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the local segment gradient ΔV / ΔI instead of the static ratio V / I defining electrical resistance.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the ratio to I / V (conductance in S) rather than V / I.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates the low-current resistance near the origin rather than at the specified operating current.

items.stem: To estimate gradient uncertainty in an optical photodiode irradiance calibration, a student draws the steepest acceptable line of worst fit between the extreme error-bar vertices at incident power 2.0 mW and 10.0 mW, as plotted. What is the gradient m_worst of this worst-fit line?
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 2 mW, y₁ = 6 μA; at x₂ = 10 mW, y₂ = 38 μA. Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (38 − 6) / (10 − 2) = 4.00 μA mW⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (38 − 6) / (10 − 2) = 4.00 μA mW⁻¹ (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts y₁ in the numerator but divides by x₂ instead of the horizontal span (x₂ − x₁).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δx / Δy instead of evaluating Δy / Δx.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the secant y₂ / x₂ as though the worst-fit line passed through the origin (0, 0) rather than (x₁, y₁).

items.stem: The suppressed-origin graph shows measurements for a tensioned constantan test wire. Two widely separated read-off points on the line of best fit have coordinates (20.0 N, 2.760 mm) and (60.0 N, 4.840 mm). What is the best-fit gradient of the graph?
items.workedSolution: Using the large triangle spanning more than half the grid: gradient = (4.840 − 2.760) / (60.0 − 20.0) = 0.05200 mm N⁻¹ ≈ 0.0520 mm N⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Calculates best-fit gradient = 0.0520 mm N⁻¹ from Δy / Δx.

items.stem: How steep (in m s⁻²) is the linear v² versus s graph recorded over 2.5 m for an air-bearing carriage coasting down a Precision granite incline on a smooth slope (sin θ = 0.2, g = 9.8 m s⁻²)?
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² and at s = 2.5 m, v² = 12.6 m² s⁻². Gradient = (12.6 − 2.8) / 2.5 = 2(9.8)(0.2) = 3.92 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 2.8 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.8 × 0.2) to get 3.92 m s⁻² (C).

items.stem: The displacement–time graph shows a laser-tracked precision stage moving on a metrology rail from t = 0.0 s to t = 20.0 s. What is its velocity during the initial stage from t = 0.0 s to t = 5.0 s?
items.workedSolution: At t = 0.0 s, s₀ = 20 m; at t = 5 s, s₁ = 65 m. Velocity v = Δs / Δt = (65 − 20) / 5 = 9.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts initial position s₀ = 20 m to obtain v = (65 − 20) / 5 = 9.00 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: A student plots current I (y-axis) against potential difference V (x-axis) for a uniform stainless steel wire of length 1.80 m and cross-sectional area 8.10 × 10⁻⁸ m². The straight line of best fit passes through the origin and the point (8.00 V, 0.500 A). What is the resistivity of the stainless steel?
items.workedSolution: Gradient m = ΔI / ΔV = 0.5000 A / 8.000 V = 0.06250 A V⁻¹. Since gradient = 1/R, R = 1/m = 16.00 Ω. Therefore ρ = R A / L = 7.200 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m ≈ 7.20 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses R = 1 / gradient and ρ = R A / L to obtain 7.20 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m.

items.stem: A tensile test on a helical steel launcher spring yields the linear force–extension plot up to 0.4 m. Calculate the elastic energy stored when extended by 0.4 m.
items.workedSolution: Elastic potential energy equals the triangular area under the F–x line: E_p = ½ F x = ½(60)(0.4) = 12.0 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes triangular area ½(60)(0.4) = 12.0 J (A).

items.stem: Between t = 7.0 s and t = 10.0 s, a reverse thrust acts on an underwater ROV thruster sled along a taut calibration tether. Determine the acceleration indicated by the velocity–time plot.
items.workedSolution: Between t = 7 s and t = 10 s, velocity changes from +20 m s⁻¹ to −10 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−10 − 20) / (10 − 7) = -10.0 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−10 − 20) / (3) = -10.0 m s⁻² (A).

items.stem: A stator current pulse acts for 0.8 s in the direction of motion of a linear-motor launch shuttle (mass 2.0 kg, initial momentum 6.0 kg m s⁻¹). Using the plotted force–time profile, determine Δv.
items.workedSolution: Impulse J = area under F–t trapezium = ½(0.8 + 0.4)(50) = 30.0 N s. Speed increase Δv = J / m = 30.0 / 2 = 15.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes J = 30.0 N s and Δv = J / 2 = 15.0 m s⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: The graph shows two I–V curves (Curve P and Curve Q) obtained for a temperature-probe element under two different physical conditions, with current I plotted on the vertical axis and potential difference V on the horizontal axis. Which statement best explains the behaviour of this component?
items.workedSolution: On an I–V graph (I on the vertical axis, V on the horizontal axis), gradient equals reciprocal of resistance. For this negative temperature coefficient thermistor, resistance decreases as temperature increases because more charge carriers are released so the curve becomes steeper.

options.label: A
options.text: Resistance increases as temperature increases because lattice vibrations block every carrier.
options.distractorRationale: Describes a metallic filament rather than an NTC semiconductor thermistor.

options.label: B
options.text: Resistance stays strictly constant at all temperatures because both curves are straight lines.
options.distractorRationale: A steeper I–V gradient means a smaller resistance, not constant resistance.

options.label: C
options.text: Curve Q represents the hotter state because a shallower I–V gradient indicates lower resistance.
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the meaning of I–V gradient (gradient equals reciprocal of resistance).

options.label: D
options.text: It exhibits resistance decreases as temperature increases because more charge carriers are released so the curve becomes steeper.

items.stem: The straight-line charging graph for an audio-filter capacitor extends from (0, 0) to a final state of Q = 2.50 mC and V = 10.0 V. Using the area under the graph, what is the electrical energy stored in the capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Triangular area under the linear graph gives E = ½ Q V = 0.5 × (2.5 × 10⁻³ C) × 10 V = 0.01250 J ≈ 0.0125 J.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly converts mC to C and obtains 0.0125 J.

items.stem: Given that a centrifuge carrier pod has velocity 14.0 m s⁻¹ tangentially forward when t = 0.0 s, use the 12.0 s acceleration–time plot to find its maximum speed.
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 6 s). Positive area Δv_max = (2)(6) + ½(4)(6) = 24.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 14 + 24.0 = 38.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 6 s (24.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 14 m s⁻¹ to get 38.0 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Evaluate the net work done by the resultant force on a cable-towed hydroplane model (mass 3.0 kg, initial speed 6.0 m s⁻¹) between x = 0.0 m and x = 15.0 m using the graph.
items.workedSolution: Forward work (0 to 12 m) = 162 J; resistive work (12 m to 15 m) = −9.00 J. Net work = 162 − 9.00 = 153 J.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts resistive triangle (9.00 J) from positive trapezium (162 J) to get 153 J (C).

items.stem: The graph displays the linear momentum of a low-friction dynamics trolley (mass 3.2 kg) against time. What resultant force acts on it between t = 3.0 s and t = 8.0 s?
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (22.4 − 6.4) / (8 − 3) = 3.20 N.

items.stem: Inspect the linear plot of measured resistance R versus L / A (spanning 0.0 m⁻¹ to 160.0 m⁻¹) for a carbon-loaded antistatic composite bar. What is the material's resistivity ρ?
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (20 − 4) / 160 = 0.100 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 4 Ω to obtain ρ = (20 − 4) / 160 = 0.100 Ω m (A).

items.stem: A variable load resistor is connected across a lithium-iron-phosphate storage cell, and the terminal potential difference V is plotted against current I up to 2.0 A. According to V = ε − Ir, what is the signed gradient of this graph?
items.workedSolution: At I = 0.0 A, V = ε = 6 V; at I = 2 A, V = 2.4 V. Gradient = (2.4 − 6) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (equal to −r).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates (2.4 − 6) / 2 = -1.80 V A⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: A capacitor in an oscilloscope capture setup discharges through a resistor R = 30 kΩ. The straight-line graph of ln(V / V) against t passes through (0 s, 2.197) and (24 s, 0.197). What is the capacitance of the capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Gradient m = (0.197 − 2.197) / (24 − 0) = -0.08333 s⁻¹. Time constant τ = −1/m = 12.00 s. Capacitance C = τ / R = 12.00 s / (30 × 10³ Ω) = 400 μF.

markScheme.criterion: Extracts linearized graph parameters accurately to obtain 400 μF.

items.stem: Starting 12.0 m beyond the base-camp beacon at t = 0.0 s, a solar-powered desert research rover executes the 8.0 s velocity–time profile shown. How far from the base-camp beacon does it come to rest?
items.workedSolution: Displacement during the 8 s run equals the trapezium area: Δx = ½(8 + 4)(8) = 48.0 m. Final position from the base-camp beacon = x₀ + Δx = 12 + 48.0 = 60.0 m.

markScheme.criterion: Adds trapezium area (48.0 m) to initial offset (12 m) to get 60.0 m (A).

items.stem: The stress–strain graph shows a high-density polyethylene filament stretched reversibly through two piecewise-linear stages up to strain 0.6 (kink at strain 0.3). What work is done per unit volume in stretching the specimen to strain 0.6?
items.workedSolution: Work per unit volume equals area under the σ–ε graph (1 MPa × 1 = 1 MJ m⁻³): u = ½(0.3)(180) + ½(180 + 250)(0.3) = 91.5 MJ m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Sums triangle and trapezium areas under σ–ε curve to obtain 91.5 MJ m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: Subtracting the constant zero-offset intercept on the F versus r⁻² plot (0.0 m⁻² to 50.0 m⁻²) for precision electrostatic spheres on a sapphire-pivot balance, find the gradient in N m².
items.workedSolution: At r⁻² = 0.0 m⁻², tare offset F₀ = 0.3 N; at r⁻² = 50 m⁻², F = 1.9 N. Gradient = (1.9 − 0.3) / 50 = 0.0320 N m².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts tare offset F₀ = 0.3 N to get (1.9 − 0.3) / 50 = 0.0320 N m² (B).

items.stem: How many ohms of static resistance does a silicon-carbide varistor element present when driven at a direct current of 2.4 A according to the V–I curve?
items.workedSolution: Electrical resistance at an operating point is defined by R = V / I (not the local slope ΔV / ΔI). At I = 2.4 A, V = 14.4 V, so R = 14.4 / 2.4 = 6.00 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Uses static ratio R = V / I = 14.4 / 2.4 = 6.00 Ω (B).

items.stem: Inspect the steepest error-bar line of worst fit plotted from 1.0 m to 6.0 m for a simple-pendulum linearization study. What value does its gradient take?
items.workedSolution: At x₁ = 1 m, y₁ = 3 s²; at x₂ = 6 m, y₂ = 26 s². Worst-fit gradient m_worst = (26 − 3) / (6 − 1) = 4.60 s² m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δy / Δx = (26 − 3) / (6 − 1) = 4.60 s² m⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: On the suppressed-origin plot for the phosphor-bronze dynamometer coil, the best-fit gradient obtained from the large triangle between 6.0 N and 22.0 N is Δy / Δx = 0.01320 m N⁻¹. What is the reciprocal constant (1 / gradient) corresponding to stiffness?
items.workedSolution: Because the axes plot length against load, stiffness k = 1 / gradient = 1 / 0.01320 = 75.76 N m⁻¹ ≈ 75.8 N m⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Computes reciprocal constant 1 / gradient = 75.8 N m⁻¹.

items.stem: Examine the straight-line plot of v² against track distance s up to 2.0 m for an optical-interruptor sled coasting down an inclined bench (ramp sin θ = 0.4, g = 9.81 m s⁻²). Evaluate its gradient.
items.workedSolution: From v² = u₀² + (2g sin θ)s, the vertical intercept is u₀² = 4 m² s⁻² and at s = 2 m, v² = 19.696 m² s⁻². Gradient = (19.696 − 4) / 2 = 2(9.81)(0.4) = 7.85 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept u₀² = 4 m² s⁻² (or evaluates 2 × 9.81 × 0.4) to get 7.85 m s⁻² (C).

options.distractorRationale: Inverts Δs / Δ(v²) instead of computing Δ(v²) / Δs.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates the secant v_max² / s_max without subtracting the non-zero intercept u₀² at s = 0.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Reports the acceleration a = g sin θ instead of the gradient 2a of the v²–s line.

items.stem: Position data for a robotic welding torch carriage on a linear gantry are plotted against time. Determine the instantaneous velocity during the outward stage between t = 0.0 s and t = 4.0 s.
items.workedSolution: At t = 0.0 s, s₀ = 14 m; at t = 4 s, s₁ = 42 m. Velocity v = Δs / Δt = (42 − 14) / 4 = 7.00 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts initial position s₀ = 14 m to obtain v = (42 − 14) / 4 = 7.00 m s⁻¹ (A).

options.distractorRationale: Computes the reciprocal Δt / Δs instead of the displacement–time gradient Δs / Δt.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides s(t₁) by t₁ without subtracting the non-zero initial displacement s₀ at t = 0.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds the initial and plateau displacements instead of taking their difference Δs.

items.stem: A student plots current I (y-axis) against potential difference V (x-axis) for a uniform nichrome-80 wire of length 1.40 m and cross-sectional area 7.70 × 10⁻⁸ m². The straight line of best fit passes through the origin and the point (10.0 V, 0.500 A). What is the resistivity of the nichrome-80?
items.workedSolution: Gradient m = ΔI / ΔV = 0.5000 A / 10.00 V = 0.05000 A V⁻¹. Since gradient = 1/R, R = 1/m = 20.00 Ω. Therefore ρ = R A / L = 1.100 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m ≈ 1.10 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses R = 1 / gradient and ρ = R A / L to obtain 1.10 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m.

items.stem: A tensile test on an optical-mount preload spring yields the linear force–extension plot up to 0.8 m. Calculate the elastic energy stored when extended by 0.8 m.
items.workedSolution: Elastic potential energy equals the triangular area under the F–x line: E_p = ½ F x = ½(68)(0.8) = 27.2 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes triangular area ½(68)(0.8) = 27.2 J (D).

items.stem: Background-corrected count rates from a radon progeny filter sample are recorded with a solid-state silicon alpha spectrometer over 50.0 s. The linearized graph plots ln(C / s⁻¹) against time t according to ln C = ln C₀ − λt. What is the gradient of this best-fit line?
items.workedSolution: At t = 0.0 s, ln C₀ = 9; at t = 50 s, ln C = 4. Gradient = (4 − 9) / 50 = -0.100 s⁻¹.

items.stem: Between t = 6.0 s and t = 10.0 s, a reverse thrust acts on a drop-tower counterbalance carriage inside a vertical guide shaft. Determine the acceleration indicated by the velocity–time plot.
items.workedSolution: Between t = 6 s and t = 10 s, velocity changes from +9 m s⁻¹ to −3 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a = Δv / Δt = (−3 − 9) / (10 − 6) = -3.00 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δv / Δt = (−3 − 9) / (4) = -3.00 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: During a 2.0 s solenoid kicker stroke, a robotic soccer puck (mass 4.0 kg, initial momentum 12.0 kg m s⁻¹) experiences the force–time profile shown. What is the time-averaged resultant force over the 2.0 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Total impulse J = ½(2 + 1)(32) = 48.0 N s. Mean force F_mean = J / Δt = 48.0 / 2 = 24.0 N.

markScheme.criterion: Divides impulse (48.0 N s) by 2 s to obtain 24.0 N (B).

items.stem: The I–V characteristic graph for an oven safety thermistor highlights an operating point where V = 6.00 V and I = 0.500 A. What is the static resistance of the component at this operating point?
items.workedSolution: Static resistance at any point on an I–V graph is R = V / I = 6.000 V / 0.5000 A = 12.00 Ω ≈ 12.0 Ω.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates R = V / I accurately to obtain 12.0 Ω.

items.stem: The charging graph for a high-voltage film capacitor is a straight line from the origin to Q = 7.20 mC at V = 24.0 V. What is the capacitance of the capacitor?
items.workedSolution: Convert Q = 7.2 mC = 7.200 × 10⁻³ C. Capacitance C = Q / V = 3.000 × 10⁻⁴ F = 300 μF.

markScheme.criterion: Correctly converts mC to C and obtains 300 μF.

items.stem: At t = 0.0 s, a centrifuge carrier pod is already moving tangentially forward at 13.0 m s⁻¹. Its signed acceleration over the next 16.0 s (tangentially forward positive) is plotted. What maximum speed does it reach during the 16.0 s interval?
items.workedSolution: Speed increases while a > 0 (from t = 0.0 s until a = 0 at t = 10 s). Positive area Δv_max = (4)(5) + ½(6)(5) = 35.0 m s⁻¹. Maximum speed = u₀ + Δv_max = 13 + 35.0 = 48.0 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Integrates positive acceleration up to t = 10 s (35.0 m s⁻¹) and adds 13 m s⁻¹ to get 48.0 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The resultant force in the direction of motion of a linear dynamo test sled (mass 3.2 kg, initial speed 4.0 m s⁻¹) is plotted over 14.0 m. Determine its speed at x = 14.0 m.
items.workedSolution: Positive work (0 to 11 m) = ½(11 + 6)(16) = 136 J. Resistive work (11 m to 14 m) = −½(3)(4) = −6.00 J. Net work W = 130 J. From ½mv² = ½mu₀² + W, v = √(4² + 2 × 130 / 3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Finds net work W = 130 J and v = √(4² + 2W/3.2) = 9.86 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Motion sensors track the momentum of a satellite attitude-test mass of mass 3.2 kg. Determine the magnitude of the resultant force acting from t = 3.0 s to t = 8.0 s.
items.workedSolution: By Newton's second law, F = Δp / Δt = (22.4 − 6.4) / (8 − 3) = 3.20 N.

items.stem: Eliminating the constant probe-lead offset from the R versus L / A graph (plotted to 400.0 m⁻¹), find the resistivity ρ of a doped silicon bar.
items.workedSolution: Since R = ρ(L / A) + R₀, resistivity ρ equals the gradient ΔR / Δ(L / A) = (30 − 6) / 400 = 0.0600 Ω m.

markScheme.criterion: Subtracts intercept R₀ = 6 Ω to obtain ρ = (30 − 6) / 400 = 0.0600 Ω m (D).

items.stem: Inspect the linear discharge characteristic V versus I (0.0 A to 2.5 A) for an alkaline lantern battery. What is the mean value of V across this interval?
items.workedSolution: Terminal p.d. varies linearly from 10 V at I = 0.0 A to 4 V at I = 2.5 A, so V_mean = ½(10 + 4) = 7.00 V.

markScheme.criterion: Averages endpoint voltages ½(10 + 4) = 7.00 V (D).
